office_does: Ferry County's three commissioners set the county budget and policy; each lives in and is nominated by a district, but the whole county elects every commissioner in the general.
race_blurb: One-term Commissioner Bob Dean, a retired Air Force and commercial flight engineer who runs on fiscal responsibility, faces Army veteran and long-haul trucker Kevin J. Berry, who runs on local jobs, small businesses and roads; both prefer the Republican Party. Berry led the District 2 primary with 539 votes to Dean's 294.

candidates.summary: Army veteran and 25-year truck driver who grew up around Curlew and returned to Ferry County in 2006; first run for office.
highlights: Nine years in the Army from 1985; RV dealership manager; 25 years as a truck driver [S1]
Would support local jobs and small businesses and maintain roads and critical infrastructure [S1]
Led the District 2 primary with 539 votes to Dean's 294 [S2]

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience, challenging the incumbent as a 'hands-on problem solver'; he does not frame the race as a call for change, so the case is partial.

candidates.summary: District 2 commissioner since winning the seat in 2022; a U.S. Army and Air Force veteran and former commercial flight engineer who sits on several regional boards.
highlights: Won the seat in 2022, 1,632 to 1,571; asks voters to 'continue the progress made' [S1][S3]
Says he focuses on contract negotiations and fiscal responsibility and backs 'government efficiency' [S1]
County member of the EMS District No. 1 board and of health, economic-development and risk boards [S1][S2]

experience.basis: One-term incumbent running explicitly on continuity ('continue the progress made'); a single term is a shorter record than a long-tenure case.

spending.basis: Stresses 'the importance of every taxpayer dollar', fiscal responsibility and 'government efficiency that respects ... your tax dollars', without proposing specific cuts.
